conflicts.subject: post
conflicts.detail: Post primary keys differ (A: uuid, B: integer)
solutions: Pick one key type for the merged entity and re-key the other source's rows
Keep a legacy_id column holding the old key during migration
conflicts.recommended: Use one key type (uuid is usual for merged data) and add a legacy_id column while migrating

resolution.decision: uuid primary key for every post (A's type). B's integer post ids are kept in legacy_id (with imported_from = 'B') during any import; nothing is re-keyed until a migration is separately approved.

conflicts.subject: user
conflicts.detail: User primary keys differ (A: uuid, B: integer)
solutions: Pick one key type for the merged entity and re-key the other source's rows
Keep a legacy_id column holding the old key during migration
conflicts.recommended: Use one key type (uuid is usual for merged data) and add a legacy_id column while migrating

resolution.decision: uuid primary key for every user (A's type). B's integer user ids kept in legacy_id (imported_from = 'B') during any import.

conflicts.subject: GET /api/posts/{} response
conflicts.detail: GET /api/posts/{} response fields disagree (id: A uuid, B integer)
solutions: Define one request and response shape and convert at the edges
Version the endpoint if existing clients need the old shape
conflicts.recommended: One contract per endpoint, written into the API spec

resolution.decision: One contract: GET /api/v1/posts/{id} returns {id: uuid string, body, status, author: {id, display_name} or null for imported anonymous posts, created_at: UTC ISO 8601}. Integer ids are not accepted.

conflicts.subject: POST /api/posts response
conflicts.detail: POST /api/posts response fields disagree (id: A uuid, B integer)
solutions: Define one request and response shape and convert at the edges
Version the endpoint if existing clients need the old shape
conflicts.recommended: One contract per endpoint, written into the API spec

resolution.decision: One contract: POST /api/v1/posts {body} returns 201 with the same post shape as GET.

conflicts.subject: GET /api/posts/{}
conflicts.detail: GET /api/posts/{} uses different auth (A: session, B: none)
solutions: Put every endpoint behind the one auth system the architecture chooses
conflicts.recommended: Same auth scheme for every endpoint

resolution.decision: One auth scheme (cookie session). Reading needs no session for a published post; a pending or rejected post needs the session of its author or a moderator, otherwise 404.

conflicts.subject: POST /api/posts
conflicts.detail: POST /api/posts uses different auth (A: session, B: optional bearer token)
solutions: Put every endpoint behind the one auth system the architecture chooses
conflicts.recommended: Same auth scheme for every endpoint

resolution.decision: Cookie session required (A). No bearer tokens, no anonymous posting (M07 deferred): without a session the answer is 401.

conflicts.subject: model
conflicts.detail: Authorization models differ (A: role-based; B: role claim in token (no permission checks in the code shown))
solutions: Choose one authorization model and express the others' rules in it
conflicts.recommended: One authorization model with one permission check function

resolution.decision: One role-based model with explicit permissions and one function can(user, action, post) used by every route and query.

conflicts.subject: max_post_length
conflicts.detail: Rule max_post_length differs (A: 5000, B: 10000)
solutions: Choose one value and record why
Make it a setting if both are legitimate
conflicts.recommended: Pick one value with the user; make it configurable only if both are needed

resolution.decision: 10000 characters for everyone (B's value). Reason: it keeps every existing post from both apps valid (5000 would reject B posts over 5000), and every post is reviewed before it is visible. Enforced in the handler (422) and by a check constraint.

conflicts.subject: read_requires_account
conflicts.detail: Rule read_requires_account differs (A: true, B: false)
solutions: Choose one value and record why
Make it a setting if both are legitimate
conflicts.recommended: Pick one value with the user; make it configurable only if both are needed

resolution.decision: Published posts are public (B); pending and rejected posts are visible only to their author and moderators; everyone else gets 404. Fixes A's leak of unreviewed posts to every member.

conflicts.subject: roles
conflicts.detail: Role sets differ (A: member, moderator; B: admin, user)
solutions: Map every source role to a unified role set and write the mapping down
Model special powers (such as approving) as permissions, not extra roles
conflicts.recommended: One role set plus explicit permissions; map every source role

resolution.decision: Unified roles member and moderator; moderate-posts is a permission of moderator. Mapping: A:member -> member, A:moderator -> moderator, B:user -> member, B:admin -> member (B's admin has no observed powers; an existing moderator promotes individual people by hand).

conflicts.subject: /login
conflicts.detail: Route /login is used by A: A-S03, B: B-S02
solutions: Merge both screens into one page with sections
Move one to a different path
conflicts.recommended: One route per screen in the unified navigation

resolution.decision: One Login screen at /login.

conflicts.subject: /posts
conflicts.detail: Route /posts is used by A: A-S01, B: B-S01
solutions: Merge both screens into one page with sections
Move one to a different path
conflicts.recommended: One route per screen in the unified navigation

resolution.decision: One PostList screen at /posts (published posts).

conflicts.subject: session
conflicts.detail: Session mechanisms differ (A: cookie session; B: jwt bearer token)
solutions: Choose one session mechanism (http-only cookie sessions are the safer default for web apps)
Use tokens only where a client cannot hold cookies
conflicts.recommended: One session mechanism for the whole app

resolution.decision: Server-side session in an http-only, secure, SameSite=Lax cookie with expiry; no JWT. B's token code and its hard-coded key are not carried over; existing B tokens stop working and B users sign in again.

conflicts.subject: imported-anonymous-posts
conflicts.detail: B allows posts with no author (author_id null, B-F04); the unified Post requires an author for new posts (A-F02) and anonymous posting is deferred (M07). Imported anonymous B posts would be rejected by a NOT NULL author.
solutions: Allow a null author only on imported B rows (check: author_id is not null or imported_from = 'B')
Assign imported anonymous posts to one placeholder account
Skip anonymous B posts on import (data loss)
conflicts.recommended: Allow a null author only on imported B rows, enforced by a check constraint; new posts always need an author

resolution.decision: author_id may be null only on imported B rows: check (author_id is not null or imported_from = 'B'). New posts always need an author.

conflicts.subject: imported-post-status
conflicts.detail: B's posts have no status and are all live (B-F03); the unified Post requires a status and every new post starts pending (A-F04). If B's existing posts are imported, they need a status, and the choice decides whether they stay visible.
solutions: Import B's posts as published, marked imported_from = B, so they stay visible; moderators may reject any later
Import B's posts as pending so moderators re-review everything (they disappear from public view until reviewed)
Do not import B's posts
conflicts.recommended: Import as published with imported_from = B; they were already public, and moderators can reject any of them

resolution.decision: Import B's posts as published with imported_from = 'B' (they were already public); moderators may reject any later.

conflicts.subject: user.role
conflicts.detail: User.role allows different values (A only: member, moderator; B only: admin, user; 4 values in all)
solutions: Define one value set and a mapping from every source value to it
Keep the field per source if the states really differ
conflicts.recommended: One value set with an explicit mapping; values without a mapping block the migration

resolution.decision: Value set {member, moderator}; mapping as in application:roles:roles. No source value is left unmapped.

conflicts.subject: post.author_id
conflicts.detail: Post.author_id types differ (A: uuid, B: integer)
solutions: Choose the wider type and convert the narrower data
Split into two fields if they mean different things
conflicts.recommended: One type per field; convert in a migration

resolution.decision: uuid referencing User.id; B's integer author ids are rewritten through the users' legacy_id map on import.

conflicts.subject: post.id
conflicts.detail: Post.id types differ (A: uuid, B: integer)
solutions: Choose the wider type and convert the narrower data
Split into two fields if they mean different things
conflicts.recommended: One type per field; convert in a migration

resolution.decision: uuid (see database:primary-key:post).

conflicts.subject: user.id
conflicts.detail: User.id types differ (A: uuid, B: integer)
solutions: Choose the wider type and convert the narrower data
Split into two fields if they mean different things
conflicts.recommended: One type per field; convert in a migration

resolution.decision: uuid (see database:primary-key:user).

conflicts.subject: post.created_at.timezone
conflicts.detail: Post.created_at timezone differs (A: stored with time zone, B: not stated)
solutions: Store one unit (for example integer cents in UTC) and convert at import
Store the unit with the value
conflicts.recommended: One unit per field, converted in the migration and tested

resolution.decision: Store created_at as timestamptz in UTC. A's values are already zoned. B's naive timestamps are converted from B's server time zone, which is unknown: the import migration may not run until the user states it (open question).

conflicts.subject: GET /api/posts/{}
conflicts.detail: GET /api/posts/{} exists in A: /api/posts/:id, B: /api/posts/<int:post_id>
solutions: Keep one endpoint and adapt clients of the other
Keep both under different paths if they serve different needs
conflicts.recommended: One endpoint per job in the unified API

resolution.decision: One endpoint GET /api/v1/posts/{id} in the posts module.

conflicts.subject: POST /api/posts
conflicts.detail: POST /api/posts exists in A: /api/posts, B: /api/posts
solutions: Keep one endpoint and adapt clients of the other
Keep both under different paths if they serve different needs
conflicts.recommended: One endpoint per job in the unified API

resolution.decision: One endpoint POST /api/v1/posts in the posts module.

conflicts.subject: b-hardcoded-signing-key
conflicts.detail: B signs and verifies JWTs with a literal key in api.py (scan: 2 medium findings) and passes no algorithms list to decode. B's sign-in (M02) is dropped, but nothing from B's auth code may be carried over.
solutions: Carry over nothing from B's token code; one cookie-session system configured from environment variables
If a token API is ever needed, a new key from the environment with a fixed algorithm and expiry
conflicts.recommended: Carry over nothing from B's token code; existing B tokens stop working after the merge and B users sign in again

resolution.decision: Nothing from B's token code is reused; every secret comes from environment variables named in .env.example.

conflicts.subject: post
conflicts.detail: Post exists in A:Post, B:Post; fields not shared: status (only A)
solutions: Merge into one table holding the fields kept features need
Keep separate tables if the two only share a name, and rename one
conflicts.recommended: Merge only once it is confirmed they mean the same thing; then list every field's origin in architecture.json

resolution.decision: Merge: A's and B's Post are the same thing (a forum post). One Post table; fields' origins listed in architecture.json.

conflicts.subject: user
conflicts.detail: User exists in A:User, B:User
solutions: Merge into one table holding the fields kept features need
Keep separate tables if the two only share a name, and rename one
conflicts.recommended: Merge only once it is confirmed they mean the same thing; then list every field's origin in architecture.json

resolution.decision: Merge: same meaning (a person who signs in). One User table; B's name maps to display_name (aliases.json).

conflicts.subject: post.author_id
conflicts.detail: Post.author_id is A: required, B: optional
solutions: Keep the field nullable
Make it required with a default for rows that have no value
conflicts.recommended: Do not make a field required until every source row has a value or a default is agreed

resolution.decision: Required for new posts; null only for imported anonymous B posts (see database:data:imported-anonymous-posts).
